disagreements.note: S1 was read twice with the same fixtures and the same two checkers. The first reading required all four I5 fixtures to differ under v0.9.4; the runbook and the Maker's pending-events note both say three, because a fixture that conforms under both checkers does not differ. The first reading therefore read does_not_conform and the second reads conforms. Recorded, never averaged; the second is the runbook's rule.
Sessions differ: some are counted and meet both thresholds, some are not counted because they read a control wrong. Outcomes are never averaged.

This record was built by build_record_v095.py, pinned by sha256 in the job log's correction note, not by the runbook's make_record.py, because the check events were logged without score, failureCondition, evidence and unobserved, and that builder copies an event's data through unchanged.

The first cycle-3 attempt is void, ratified by the Owner: a planted control's evidence value was rewritten with a placeholder digest, so the control never validated and all nine sessions were disqualified by it. That attempt produced no result and is not a cycle; cycle 3 was re-run from scratch on twelve fresh records. The void was declared after all nine sessions of that attempt had run and been scored.

Stranger-test readings were filed under ORCH-SCRIPT when they were logged; this record files each under its implementer, with a batch per session holding that session's planted and clean controls. The correction is recorded here, not hidden.

The first packages of this release overwrote v0.9.4's published CHANGELOG history (a finishing-script defect, found after the first disposition); this package restores it and the first disposition was withdrawn.
S3's sessions read the package of event 43, which differs from this one only in CHANGELOG.md and record/; S3's checks are re-filed against this package, not re-run.

Each implementer's endpoint is the API host of the provider its harness files name as having answered (Seed, MiniMax, BaseTen). The harness records the provider, not a host, and the mapping from provider to host is the Orchestrator's.
The Orchestrator authored the S1, S2 and S3 instruments and also assembles this record; the readings are filed under ORCH-SCRIPT and under each implementer, never under the Orchestrator.
S1 was read twice; the first reading used a rule stricter than the runbook's, and the disagreement is recorded rather than averaged (CL1-10).
Nemotron 3 Ultra is unobserved: none of its three sessions was counted.
The stranger test passed in cycle 3 with two implementers observed and both meeting the bar; cycles 1 and 2 did not pass (see record/STRANGER-TEST-v0.9.5.md).
